atlas-pl.0073: Student work is the norm and the rules favour it: a student under 26 on an umowa zlecenie pays no social or health contributions, income up to PLN 85,528 a year is exempt from income tax for under-26s, and Warsaw University of Technology says 44% of its graduates had a job before graduating. Foreign students on full-time courses can work without a permit.
atlas-pl.0074: University career offices and job fairs
atlas-pl.0075: The University of Warsaw Career Office lists faculty-level fairs: Psychological Career Days on 13 to 15 October 2026, the Faculty of Management career day on 20 and 21 October and an IT job fair at the Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Mechanics on 28 October; past years added a language fair and a public-sector career day in May.
atlas-pl.0077: Poland’s IT market is large but junior-thin: of about 111,000 IT postings on Just Join IT in 2025, juniors were 4.79%, while juniors apply about twice as often as experienced candidates. On 8 October 2026 the board showed 668 junior offers among 19,988.
atlas-pl.0078: Foreign arrivals add competition: Bending Spoons opened a Warsaw office in September 2026 and reports about 50,000 applications from Poland in the first nine months of the year.
atlas-pl.0079: Civil-service competitions and the public job board
atlas-pl.0080: The Civil Service job board listed 413 offers from 202 offices in 103 towns on 8 October 2026; you apply to the office that advertises, and a filter shows which offers are open to foreigners.
atlas-pl.0081: Open ads, portals and public employment services (the experienced hire)
atlas-pl.0082: Experienced candidates apply to open ads on the tech board Just Join IT (where mid-level and senior offers are 6,621 and 11,386 against 668 junior), on company career pages and through the public employment services, which run Zielona Linia.
atlas-pl.0083: Automation and a maturing sector are thinning the junior rung: process automation runs in 74.1% of centres and the junior share is falling, while the middle widens.
atlas-pl.0084: ABSL’s 2025 report put the centres’ headcount up 6.2% on the year, and 61 centres opened between January 2024 and March 2025, mostly in IT (42.6%) and R&D (26.2%).
atlas-pl.0085: Western banks’ Polish centres (Goldman Sachs and others in Warsaw, HSBC in Kraków) hire graduates into risk, finance operations and engineering, not client-facing deal roles; local banks such as PKO recruit in Polish and run branch, risk (zaRyzykuj), corporate-client and ESG internship tracks.
atlas-pl.0086: The Big Four take interns every year: KPMG’s World of Audit offers a paid full-time audit internship in 7 offices from January, EY hires audit and tax interns with online tests, and PwC recruits in four stages including an assessment centre. In 2010 the press counted 100 to 200 interns per firm.
atlas-pl.0087: Deloitte Poland lists advisory, consulting, audit, tax, legal and its Central Europe business-services centre as the areas open to students and graduates; its page promises a transparent process but gives no stages.
atlas-pl.0088: The service centres hire business graduates into finance operations, procurement and customer operations; the language allowance (PLN 600 to 2,000 a month) makes a second language part of the pay.
atlas-pl.0089: Poland’s IT market is large but junior-thin: of about 111,000 IT postings on Just Join IT in 2025, juniors were 4.79%, while juniors apply about twice as often as experienced candidates. Warsaw University of Technology says 44% of its graduates had a job before graduating.
atlas-pl.0090: PwC’s three-month summer programme offers nine technology paths with a mentor, and KPMG’s online tests cover numerical and verbal reasoning and English.
atlas-pl.0091: The state hires through the Civil Service board (413 offers on 8 October 2026), and the University of Warsaw has held a public-sector career day in May to explain internships and recruitment.
atlas-pl.0092: Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and the other university cities feed their local centres and banks through faculty career days and job fairs; the University of Warsaw’s career office lists them by faculty (management, psychology, IT, languages).
atlas-pl.0093: University of Warsaw, autumn 2026: Psychological Career Days 13 to 15 October, Faculty of Management career day 20 and 21 October, IT job fair 28 October.
atlas-pl.0094: KPMG’s World of Audit runs three workshops on 8, 15 and 22 October (the last online) before it guarantees an internship offer.
atlas-pl.0095: No single national season; programmes keep their own calendars. PKO recruited for its July to September internship from 7 May 2026, PwC’s summer programme runs July to September and was closed to new applicants, KPMG’s World of Audit workshops are in October for a January internship, and university fairs cluster in October and March.
atlas-pl.0096: The programmes we read start at the student stage: KPMG’s World of Audit takes students from their 4th year or graduates, PKO takes students and graduates, and nobody asks for a master’s. The centres hire for languages, not for degree level.
atlas-pl.0097: Poland’s ENIC/NARIC role is held by NAWA, which took over academic recognition on 1 February 2018 and has separate pages for professional recognition, EU/OECD/EFTA degrees and regulated professions; we could not read the rules on those pages. For a non-EU Blue Card, the degree is documented with a sworn translation.
atlas-pl.0098: Employers know the leading universities (Warsaw University of Technology reports 44% of graduates already employed), but no programme we read names a target school.
atlas-pl.0099: There is no formal dual-study culture for graduates, but working during the degree is the norm: tax and contribution rules favour students under 26, and 44% of Warsaw University of Technology graduates worked before graduating.
atlas-pl.0100: The public sector is small as a graduate employer next to the service centres: 413 offers from 202 offices on the Civil Service board on 8 October 2026, against 488,700 people in the centres.
atlas-pl.0101: The centres employ many foreigners (19.6% of staff, mostly from Ukraine, India, Belarus and Italy), but an ordinary non-EU permit needs a labour-market test by the district office and a PLN 400 employer fee; graduates of Polish full-time courses are exempt from work permits. The rules are on the Visas page.
atlas-pl.0102: A photo is not required, and the Zielona Linia page says an employer who demands one would not be compliant with the Labour Code, but many recruiters like one.
atlas-pl.0103: We found no Polish page that states a CV length; a one-to-two-page CV with the data-processing clause is the safe format.
atlas-pl.0104: The portals we read (KPMG, EY, PKO) ask for an online profile or form and a CV; none mentions a cover letter.
atlas-pl.0105: We found no page that asks for references with the application.
atlas-pl.0106: Employers ask for the CV and the data-processing clause; diploma copies come at the offer stage, and a sworn translation is needed for a Blue Card or recognition.
atlas-pl.0107: Since the Labour Code amendment of June 2025, the employer must give you the pay or range in the advert, before the interview or before the contract, and may not ask what you earned in earlier jobs. We found no page on whether forms ask for your expectation.
atlas-pl.0108: We found no page on background checks in Polish graduate hiring; banks and the public sector can be expected to check more.
atlas-pl.0109: Applications work, especially at the service centres. Add a data-processing consent clause (klauzula RODO) at the foot of the CV: many recruiters expect it, and it is needed if you want to be kept for future openings.
atlas-pl.0110: KPMG’s steps are all online, PKO’s interviews are online and the tech and public boards are open to anyone; a non-EU hire from abroad still needs a permit first.
atlas-pl.0111: English is the working language in most centres and tech firms, and KPMG tests English online (a 2010 report says the same of the Big Four); Polish is needed at local banks and firms.
atlas-pl.0112: KPMG’s process has four steps, all online, with an online test of numerical reasoning, verbal reasoning and English; EY’s is an online profile (about 15 minutes), a review, online tests for students and graduates, interviews in person, by phone or video with the talent team and then the team, and an offer.
atlas-pl.0113: PKO Bank Polski’s steps are an online form with CV, a call if you meet the requirements, an online interview that may have two stages, and an answer whatever the result.
atlas-pl.0114: PwC’s page lists four stages for its internships: application, competency tests, language verification and an assessment centre. We found no page on dress or on the time from application to offer.
atlas-pl.0115: The Labour Code allows a probation contract of up to three months: one month if a fixed-term contract shorter than six months follows, two months if it is six to twelve months, three months otherwise. Notice during probation is three working days for up to two weeks, one week above that and two weeks for three months.
atlas-pl.0116: After probation the notice is two weeks below six months of service, one month from six months and three months from three years. Student and intern work is often on an umowa zlecenie rather than an employment contract; PKO’s internship is on one.
